engagement_title: Static Union autumn small goods: rebuild four label graphics as patch, pin and sticker art that each survive how the item is actually made, bind the printer's hang tag into a live twelve item run, and hand the makers and the stockists one editable set
vertical: Streetwear and fashion: an eight person independent label in Portland running two drops a year, selling direct and through roughly forty specialist stockists, moving into small goods for the first time
real_brief_anchor: The ledger carries NO posted brief for VECTOR-12 (real_brief_anchors is empty in the build batch and in PORTFOLIO_LEDGER_v2), so no quotation is invented here. The concept is anchored instead to the commission class this is: the recurring small goods pack a small apparel label posts when it moves from garments into pins, patches and stickers, where the label owns the graphics but owns them only as whatever files were sent back over three years, and where three different manufacturers have each already refused something. The ledger's own framing is kept verbatim in spirit: 'a few of our graphics as messy exports' rebuilt as 'the right kind of art for how it's actually made', with maker spec sheets, a mockup board and a woven label lockup. The REBUILD was called because the ledger concept counted only two surfaces and ended in a stack of vector files, which is one deliverable and one surface pretending to be six. The fuller commission a label actually buys before a drop is the one here: the manufacture art, the hang tag run the printer needs for twelve items, the stockist and maker collateral the label edits itself as items get pulled, and a written account of what will not work. The label is Static Union, the founder is Nils Brandt, and no real brand, person, factory or platform is referenced anywhere.
client_one_liner: Our graphics only exist as whatever files people happened to send us, the patch factory has already turned one of them down once, and I need the small goods pack plus the tags and the stockist sheet before the drop.
client_brief:
Static Union is eight people and we do two drops a year. Autumn is small goods for the first time. Enamel pins, embroidered patches and stickers, twelve items in total, going out with hang tags to about forty stockists.

Here is our actual problem. Our graphics only exist as whatever file whoever made them happened to send us. Four of them matter. Two came back from a printer, one is a photograph of a woven label because the file is gone, and one came out of an old tee artwork folder. They look fine on screen and we have been putting them on garments for two years.

The patch factory turned our first attempt down in July. They said the art was not patch art. The pin maker asked for something different again, and the sticker converter asked for something different from both. I do not fully understand the difference between the three and I am tired of learning it one rejection at a time. I want each graphic rebuilt as the right kind of art for the thing it is becoming, and I want it to stay recognisably the same mark across all three, because a pack that does not match is not a pack.

Sizes and grounds matter. Patches go on dark twill at about two and a half inches. Pins are an inch. Stickers are three inches on white vinyl. We also want a small woven label lockup for the inside of the caps.

The makers' limits are in the file I sent. Please treat those as hard, because they are the reason we got refused.

We need the hang tags too. The printer still has our tag from last season and the twelve items are in the spreadsheet, one tag per item, and I would rather not retype anything.

Last, the stockist sheet, the maker specs and the announcement squares. Those have to be in one file I can edit myself, because items get pulled and prices move right up to the drop.

What I need back: the three sets of manufacture art, the extracted graphics as clean masters, the tag run, the editable set plus whatever it was built from, a board I can send round, and a note telling me plainly what will not work and why.
price_band_and_audience: Independent streetwear small goods. Stickers 4 dollars, pins 14 dollars, patches 18 dollars, sold direct and wholesale to specialist stockists, buyers roughly 17 to 30. The band is load-bearing in a specific way: the price ladder is a fidelity ladder. The 4 dollar sticker keeps the full drawing because vinyl costs nothing to hold detail. The 18 dollar patch is deliberately reduced to bold thread blocks because thread cannot hold the drawing and because a patch that looks like a printed sticker looks cheap on a garment. So the same mark is simplified MORE as the item becomes more made, which is the exact inverse of the instinct that says the expensive item deserves more detail. The collateral follows the same logic: a specialist stockist sheet at this band is plain, dense and legible, not a luxury brochure, and the announcement squares read as a label talking to its own buyers rather than as advertising. An agent that ships one master drawing scaled three ways, or that dresses the stockist sheet up to a fashion house register, has misread the commission even if every file opens correctly. The ledger records the base concept at 600 to 1,200 dollars; this fuller commission, with the tag run and the editable set, runs 1,400 to 2,600 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Two drops a year, made to be worn out
brand_identity.sector: Independent streetwear label making garments and, from this autumn, small goods (pins, patches, stickers) for a young direct and wholesale audience.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, Portland, Oregon. An eight person independent label run out of one studio.
brand_identity.about: Static Union is a small Portland label that puts out two considered drops a year and sells them direct and through roughly forty specialist stockists. The marks came out of the founder's own hand and the early tee runs, and they have been carried on garments for two seasons. Autumn is the first move into small goods, so the same marks now have to survive being made rather than printed.
brand_identity.audience: Buyers roughly 17 to 30 who follow small labels, shop drops rather than seasons, and buy direct or from specialist streetwear stockists. They notice when a pack does not match.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Accessible independent streetwear. Stickers at 4 dollars, pins at 14, patches at 18, wholesale to about forty stockists. Priced to be cheap enough to collect and good enough to keep, never luxury.
brand_identity.typography: Display is a heavy condensed grotesque with a workwear feel, used for the label name and drop titles. Text is a plain, legible sans for stockist copy and specs. The type stays quiet so the marks lead.
brand_identity.voice: Direct, plain, a little dry, talking to its own buyers rather than advertising. A line the brand would write: "Autumn small goods. Twelve pieces, made to last, gone when they are gone."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no proper brand kit. The four marks that matter survive only as whatever files people happened to send back over three years: two came from a printer, one exists only as a photograph of a woven cap label because the file is gone, and one came out of an old tee artwork folder. They look fine on screen and have been used for two years, but there are no editable masters.
brand_identity.values: Make a small number of things properly and stand behind the drop. A pack that does not match is not a pack.

assets_supplied.name: static_union_marks/ (four graphics, 2,000 to 3,600px)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The four that matter. Two came back from a printer, one came out of an old tee artwork folder. They look flat and we have been using them for two years." The eagle and bolt device, the arc badge, the union stripe block and the small bolt icon.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the four are not flat art at all but exports of screen print separations, carrying a fine halftone dot through their solid areas and a soft gradient across one element, which is invisible at any size a person would look at them and only declares itself in what a trace returns. Nothing in the file name, the appearance or the client's account distinguishes those two from the genuinely flat pair.

assets_supplied.name: su_woven_label_photo.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The arc badge as it exists on a woven label, photographed on the bench, because that file is long gone." A 3,800px phone frame of a woven cap label lying on a cutting mat, shot slightly off axis under bench light.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The badge is a compound lockup of an arc type ring, an inner rule and a central bolt, and a single selection aimed at the whole thing returns some of those elements and silently drops others, so the mask succeeds, looks entirely plausible and is incomplete. The counters in the arc lettering are what makes the badge readable at all, and they are the first thing any route that treats the badge as one object fills in.

assets_supplied.name: su_hangtag_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The tag the printer ran for us last season, exactly as they sent it back." A press PDF of the finished hang tag face and reverse, with the item name, colourway, size, price, edition line and stockist code sitting in visually separate blocks.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The tag face was set as one continuous flow, so what a conversion exposes as separately addressable frames is nothing like the printed page suggests, and the readout of that flow omits one run while keeping its line break, so the text still looks well formed and every position past the omission is short. A validation pass on positions computed from that readout returns valid.

assets_supplied.name: su_smallgoods.csv
assets_supplied.visible_description: Twelve rows, one per item: item name, colourway, physical size, wholesale price, retail price, edition count and stockist code, in the order the printer wants them run.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The colourway names differ enough in length that on the longest rows the text simply stops at the frame edge rather than overflowing anywhere a person would notice, so the tag looks correctly set and is missing the end of a field on those records only.

assets_supplied.name: su_maker_limits.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The three makers' stated limits, in their own words: thread colour count and minimum stroke for the patch, enamel bridge and metal line minimum for the pin, kiss cut offset and minimum enclosed window for the sticker, plus the physical size and the ground each item is made on.

assets_supplied.name: su_copy.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The drop name, the twelve item descriptions, the stockist ordering blurb and the announcement wording the label posts when a drop goes live.

acceptance_bar: Each of the three media gets art built for that medium, not one drawing scaled three ways, and the pack still reads as one mark across all three.
Every maker limit in the supplied file is met as stated, including thread colour count, minimum stroke, enamel bridge, metal line minimum and minimum enclosed window.
Each piece of manufacture art is legible at its true reproduction size on its true ground, judged there and not at canvas size: patch on dark twill, pin at one inch, sticker on white vinyl.
Every delivered vector carries a viewBox and no full canvas opaque background path, so it can sit on any ground without a box behind it.
The badge lockup is complete, with its type ring, inner rule and central element all present, and its counters read as holes rather than filled.
The sticker cut line is a genuine outward offset of the art silhouette with the enclosed windows the converter asked for, and it does not slice the drawing anywhere.
The pin is delivered as separated metal line and enamel fill plates whose wells close, not as a single flattened picture.
No invented pixels anywhere. No delivered file is larger than its source and the note lists every file any tool resized or extended, and by how much.
The hang tag run is one press ready file with one item per page, twelve pages in the order the spreadsheet gives, and every field on every page is complete rather than ending early.
No tag carries a field that was silently dropped or silently cut off, and the note names any record that needed the copy shortened.
The stockist sheet, the maker specs and the announcement squares sit in ONE editable file, each keeping its own canvas size, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.
The words in that file are live text the client can retype and the marks in it are real vector artwork rather than pictures of a layout.
One type system across every canvas, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
The board carries the finished pack with nothing silently missing from it.
The note says plainly which graphic could not become which item and what to do instead, rather than shipping something the factory will refuse a second time.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle what lands where: the graphics and the plates on imaging, the tag run on the layout and merge surface, the sheets and squares on HTML authoring.
trajectory.judgement: This looks like one job and is three. The trap is treating the whole commission as vector cleanup, which produces files no maker accepts and no tags at all.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming deliverable to surface, and the confirmed tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the four graphics, the woven label photograph, the tag PDF and the spreadsheet, holding a manifest with source dimensions.
trajectory.judgement: Source dimensions are recorded here because every no invented pixels claim later is made against them.
trajectory.produces: A manifest with source dimensions per file.

trajectory.action: Preview all four graphics and the label photograph, and triage: what kind of file each actually is, how each mark is constructed, and which graphic is going to become which item.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing of graphic to item is the first irreversible craft call. The most detailed drawing is the one that fails hardest as thread, and the simplest is wasted on vinyl, so the obvious allocation is the wrong one.
trajectory.produces: A per graphic triage note and a stated graphic to item allocation.

trajectory.action: Extract each graphic to transparency: selections worded at the graphic's own visual properties rather than at the surface it sits on, inverted for polarity, cropped to the selection bounds.
trajectory.judgement: Naming the substrate pulls the selection to the substrate. Background removal is the wrong instrument on a disjoint mark with enclosed counters and will return a solid blob that reports success.
trajectory.produces: Four transparent art masters at source scale.

trajectory.action: Recover the arc badge from the woven label photograph: straighten first, then select per element and composite rather than asking for the lockup as one thing.
trajectory.judgement: A compound lockup comes back partially and plausibly, so the decision is to build it from parts and to check what is present rather than to accept the first mask that looks like a badge.
trajectory.produces: A complete badge master with its ring, rule and central element.

trajectory.action: Prepare a separate raster per medium before any tracing: flatten the visible colour regions down to the thread count the patch maker allows, keep the full drawing for the sticker, and separate the metal line from the enamel fields for the pin.
trajectory.judgement: The tracing step takes no options at all, so colour count, detail level and edge quality are decisions that have to be made entirely in the raster. Three preparations from one master, not one preparation used three times.
trajectory.produces: Medium specific prepared plates for patch, pin and sticker.

trajectory.action: Trace each prepared plate, inject a viewBox, and strip the opaque full canvas path the tracer always emits.
trajectory.judgement: Polarity decides whether the trace is a mark or a filled box, and the ground path rides along into every downstream placement if it is not removed here.
trajectory.produces: Traced plates as scalable, placeable vector art.

trajectory.action: Build the sticker cut art: the kiss cut line as an outward offset of the art silhouette, carrying the enclosed windows the converter asked for.
trajectory.judgement: Offset direction is the whole thing, and an enclosed window is only a window if the path says so rather than if it looks like one.
trajectory.produces: Sticker face art plus its cut line.

trajectory.action: Place each traced plate at its true reproduction size on its true ground and look at each one: the patch at two and a half inches on dark twill, the pin at one inch on metal, the sticker at three inches on white vinyl, the woven lockup at label width.
trajectory.judgement: This is the only place the reduction can be judged, because every plate is convincing at canvas size on white. Deciding to look at real size on the real ground is the agent's own move and nothing prompts it.
trajectory.produces: A legibility verdict per plate at its delivered size.

trajectory.action: Derive the pin's two plates from the settled art: the metal line plate and the enamel fill plate, with the bridges the maker requires between adjacent colours.
trajectory.judgement: Every enamel well has to close or the colour runs, and a bridge added for manufacture changes the drawing, so it is a design decision rather than a technical one.
trajectory.produces: Metal line and enamel fill plates for each pin.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's tag PDF, then round trip the converted document's structure and read what the tag actually exposes as addressable frames and what the true text of each frame is, before writing any mapping.
trajectory.judgement: The printed page's visual blocks are not evidence about the document's frames, and the convenient readout of a frame's text is not the same thing as the frame's text. Building the mapping from the convenient one is the fast path.
trajectory.produces: A true frame inventory and a mapping built from the reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Prepare the merge template against the spreadsheet, then round trip the result again and confirm every expected field placeholder is actually present.
trajectory.judgement: A success message from this step is not evidence that the fields landed, and a mapping validator can pass on positions that are wrong.
trajectory.produces: A verified merge template with every field confirmed present.

trajectory.action: Merge the twelve items to a press file with one item per page in spreadsheet order, then render per item proofs, and read every page rather than the first.
trajectory.judgement: Twelve pages is few enough to read and the failure mode does not announce itself in any response. Reading page one and inferring the rest is the usual error here.
trajectory.produces: A twelve page press file and per item proofs, each read.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the family style inventories for real numeric weights, launder every name, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own and has to read as an independent label talking to specialist buyers rather than as a fashion house. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name and a display cut is reached by its own family slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry or designer and real weight per role.

trajectory.action: Search Stock with short generic queries for the grounds the pack has to be shown on, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, and bring each toward one look.
trajectory.judgement: Choosing grounds whose light can be brought together rather than the best thumbnail, since a 240 pixel thumbnail is not evidence about anything.
trajectory.produces: Licensed camera scale grounds for the presentation canvases.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML with roots at several canvas sizes: a maker spec sheet per medium at true physical dimensions carrying the plates and the stated limits, the stockist line sheet with the twelve items as a real table, and the announcement squares. Place every plate as inline vector inside an explicitly sized and top left anchored wrapper, embed every photograph as image data, and declare family and weight on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph here, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, weight is not inherited from markup semantics, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole collateral set, retained as a deliverable in its own right.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per canvas markup for the rest, asserting per canvas that every plate arrived as vector shapes, every photograph resolved to real image data, and nothing resolves past its declared canvas width.
trajectory.judgement: Treating a successful export as unverified. Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning and the rendition only ever shows the first canvas.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document with every canvas, one inspected visually and the rest audited in markup.

trajectory.action: Create the board and add the finished pack, treating a partial success as partial. Then write the note: the reduction applied per medium and why, the maker limits each plate meets, every resize any tool reported, the type system, any record whose copy had to change, and a plain statement of which graphic could not become which item and what to do instead.
trajectory.judgement: The note is the deliverable the founder actually relies on, because the whole commission exists because three factories told him no without explaining. Saying what will be refused again, before it is sent, is the professional part of the job.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the tracer actually returns from a graphic that looks flat and is not. Two of the four exports came out of screen print separations and carry a fine halftone dot through their solid areas plus a soft gradient across one element. At every size a person views them at, including full screen, they are indistinguishable from the genuinely flat pair, and the colour flattening done in the raster preparation addresses the regions that can be seen and leaves the dot untouched because there is nothing visible to address. The trace of those two comes back as scores of near identical fills instead of the handful the patch maker permits, and it renders identically to the eye, so the file looks correct and the SVG is a thread specification no factory will accept. The tracer reports success, takes no options at all, and offers no readout of what it produced. There is no parameter that could have been set correctly, and which of the four graphics carries the hidden texture cannot be established before tracing them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre empt it. A careful agent flattens the visible colour regions, gets the polarity right and strips the ground path, and still gets an exploded trace on exactly the two files whose defect is invisible. (b) Nothing states it. The maker limits file states the thread count as a hard bar, which is the client passing on the factory's own constraint exactly as he would to a designer, and the brief says the July attempt was refused, which is the symptom that caused the hire. Neither says which graphics are separations, that a hidden dot exists, or that the trace will multiply it. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is to go back into the raster with masked fills that consolidate the affected areas into true solids, which is a different operation on a different principle from the reduction already done, and it changes both the patch plate and the pin's enamel field boundaries.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Return to the raster preparation and consolidate the affected areas into genuine solids with masked fills rather than trying to simplify the traced result, re trace, and re check the fill count rather than assuming the second attempt took. Then re derive the pin's enamel fields, since their boundaries came from the same prepared plate, and correct the colour list on the maker spec sheet, which was written from the first trace.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The patch factory refuses the art a second time on the same grounds, after the label paid someone specifically to stop that happening, and the pin maker quotes an enamel count that does not exist.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the reduction that satisfies the maker's limits is the same reduction that survives on the maker's ground. The plates are convincing at canvas size on white, which is the only size and ground anyone looks at them at by default. At two and a half inches on dark twill the badge's arc lettering closes its counters and the inner rule merges into the ring, so the mark reads as a filled disc with a smudge in it, and at one inch on metal the bolt's thinnest strokes fall below the metal line minimum in places the eye did not flag at full size. Both plates pass a colour count check and both look right in every file the client would be shown. Nothing measures this, no operation reports it, and the two failures are different in kind: one is legibility at size, one is a manufacturing minimum, and neither is visible until the art is placed at its delivered size on the ground it is delivered onto.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The plates have to exist before they can be placed, there is no measurement available, and no amount of care at the reduction stage substitutes for looking at the result at real size, because the reduction that meets the thread count and the reduction that stays readable in thread are not the same reduction and only the second one can be seen. (b) Nothing states it. The maker limits file gives the sizes, the grounds and the minimums, which is the constraint. The brief says the patch factory called the art not patch art, which is the client repeating a rejection he does not understand. Neither says which element closes, at which size, on which ground. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is a design decision about which detail is sacrificed to keep the mark readable at patch size, or about moving a graphic to a different item in the pack, both of which change the allocation made at triage and change what the woven label lockup can carry.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Redraw the reduction so the elements that close are opened or dropped rather than shrunk, which means going back to the raster preparation and in some cases back to the graphic to item allocation, then re place at true size on the true ground rather than assuming the heavier version worked. Check the plates that were not flagged at the same real size, since the reason to look was found on one and the others have not been established as clean. If a graphic will not hold as a patch at all, say which item it becomes instead and re author the spec sheet around it.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The label ships a patch on which its own badge is an unreadable filled disc and a pin whose thinnest strokes cannot be struck, discovers it when the sample arrives from the factory, and misses the drop date it commissioned this work to hit.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's tag actually is as a document, and what survives the merge onto twelve real records. The printed page shows the item name, colourway, price and code as visually separate blocks, but the tag face was set as one continuous flow, so what the conversion exposes bears no relation to what the page suggests, and the convenient readout of that flow omits one run while keeping its line break, leaving a string that still looks well formed and every position past the omission short by the exact length of the omitted run. A mapping built on those positions validates cleanly and the template preparation reports success while some fields never land at all. Separately, on the records whose colourway name is longest, the text simply stops at the frame edge rather than overflowing anywhere a person would notice, so a tag looks correctly set and ends mid field. None of this appears in any response. It appears on the merged pages, and only on some of them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. Frame granularity from a converted PDF is not under the agent's control and cannot be predicted from the printed page, and the truncation is a property of one field's length against one frame's width on specific records, which does not exist until those records are merged. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the printer has last season's tag and asks for one tag per item with nothing retyped, which is a client describing what he has. No asset note says the tag is one flow, that a run is omitted, or which records run long. (c) It is not a propagation re run. The response is to reconstruct the frame's true text from the document structure and recompute every position against it, which is a different method from the one the tooling steers toward, plus a copy decision about the records that will not fit, which is the client's business rather than a re export.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping from the reconstructed story text rather than the readout, re prepare the template, and confirm the placeholders are present by inspecting the document again rather than trusting the success message. Re merge and read all twelve pages, not the ones that failed before, since a corrected offset can move a different field. For the records that still end early, shorten the copy with the client's own wording from the supplied file and record which records changed.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve hang tags go to the printer with fields missing on some records and colourway names cut off mid word on others, the run is printed, and the label pays for it twice because everything the tooling said along the way said the job had succeeded.

deliverables.name: Static Union manufacture art, three media
deliverables.spec: Per graphic, three genuinely different pieces of art rather than one drawing at three sizes: an embroidery reduction within the stated thread count and minimum stroke that stays readable at patch size on dark twill, separated metal line and enamel fill plates whose wells close and whose bridges meet the pin maker's minimum, and full detail sticker face art with a true outward kiss cut line carrying the enclosed windows the converter asked for, plus the woven label lockup. Every file carries a viewBox and no full canvas opaque ground path.

deliverables.name: Extracted graphic masters
deliverables.spec: The four label graphics lifted clean off whatever file they arrived in, delivered as transparent masters at source scale with no substrate, no captured ground and no filled counters, including the compound arc badge rebuilt complete from the photographed woven label with its type ring, inner rule and central element all present. These are the single source every medium specific plate is derived from, so any drift between the patch version and the pin version traces back to here.

deliverables.name: Twelve item hang tag run
deliverables.spec: The printer's own tag artwork reverse engineered into a live merge template bound to the twelve row spreadsheet, delivered as one press ready file with one item per page in spreadsheet order, every field complete on every page, plus per item proofs the client can read before the printer does. Any record whose copy had to be shortened to fit is named in the handover rather than silently trimmed.

deliverables.name: Maker specs, stockist line sheet and announcement squares as one editable document plus its source

decision_gates: Which graphic becomes which item, given that the most detailed drawing fails hardest as thread and the simplest is wasted on vinyl.
How much detail each medium loses, and where a reduction stops being a reduction and becomes a different mark.
How to word a selection so it returns the graphic rather than the surface the graphic is printed on.
Whether to rebuild the compound badge per element or accept a single mask that looks like a badge.
How much of the preparation happens in the raster, given that the tracing step offers no controls of any kind.
Whether a plate that meets the stated limits but closes up at delivered size is fixed by opening the drawing or by moving the graphic to another item.
Where the enamel bridges go, since a bridge added for manufacture is a change to the drawing.
Whether the tag's printed blocks correspond to anything addressable in the converted document, and what to build the mapping from if they do not.
What to do about records whose copy will not fit, and whether that is the freelancer's call or the client's.
Whether to read one merged page or all twelve before sending the run.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a specialist stockist rather than a luxury buyer.
How the presentation canvases show the pack: which grounds are licensed, and whether they read as the label's own goods or as bought photography.
What to escalate in writing versus what to fix silently, on a commission whose entire premise is that three factories refused something without explaining why.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of patches. IDENTITY is the commission: these are four specific graphics a label has been putting on garments for two years, one of which now exists only as a photograph of a woven label, and a redrawn eagle or a regenerated badge is a different label's mark on the same body of customers. SPEC is manufacturing: three factories have written limits on thread count, minimum stroke, metal line width, enamel bridging and enclosed window size, and the deliverable is art that satisfies them, in separated plates, at stated physical sizes on stated grounds. A generated image satisfies none of it and cannot be checked against it, which is precisely how the label got refused in July. EDITABILITY runs through two deliverables: a merge template bound to a spreadsheet so twelve tags run without retyping, and one document with live text the founder edits as items get pulled. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this reduction still read in thread at two and a half inches, does this trace carry a colour count a factory will quote, does this converted tag expose anything the fields can attach to. None of that is a generation problem, and the note explaining which graphic will be refused again is advice a render cannot give.
doability_proof: Five surfaces, honestly counted. image_vectorize is counted inside the Photoshop and Lightroom surface, not as an Illustrator surface, and the Illustrator tools are never called because document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector sit on a polling helper that does not exist in this host. Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). IMAGING: headless upload through asset_initialize_file_upload, curl PUT and asset_finalize_file_upload, then select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, fill_area with a mask, masked adjustments, auto_straighten, remove_background and vectorize are all verified live. The verified extract and reuse chain, selection worded at the mark's own visual properties then inverted then cropped then traced, is exactly what recovers a graphic off a photographed woven label, and the verified finding that naming the substrate returns the substrate is the live gate on step 4. Compound marks are documented as returning partially and plausibly, which is why the badge is built per element. remove_background is documented as failing on disjoint marks and on enclosed interiors, so it is never the route to a counter. image_vectorize takes no options at all, emits no viewBox and always emits an opaque first path, all verified, so the raster preparation is the only lever and the hygiene is real work. crop_and_resize is documented as interpolating to a hard cap and reporting it only in the tradeoffs array, so the no invented pixels bar is scored as a decision plus a disclosure rather than as any measurement the agent takes. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are verified fully headless and synchronous end to end, including building a live merge template from a bare press PDF. One record per page is the verified PDF behaviour and page count equals row count is checkable exactly. The lossy textContent finding, where an omitted run leaves every later offset short and the validator still returns valid, is a verified live finding, as is the frame granularity finding that a continuous flow converts to a single frame. Per record proofs come from createSeparateFiles, whose order is verified correct, never from multi record raster URLs, whose order is verified reversed. No bleed gate, no pdfPreset, no variable QR, since all three are verified unavailable. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, true physical canvases resolve exactly at absolute units, real tables survive, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, and external image URLs render as empty placeholders so every photograph is embedded as image data. The right anchored auto sized wrapper failure is a verified live finding the trajectory designs against. Transport goes through the text/html upload path because embedded photography exceeds the inline threshold, and verification is split because the rendition preview shows the first canvas only. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, kit chain is verified end to end, and the non standard numeric weights, the slug not PostScript CSS rule and the all or nothing kit call are live findings the task leans on. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only, orientation never passed because it is verified broken, licensing returns genuine camera scale imagery, and boards persist with a twelve placement cap where 201 means partial success with a failed items list. VOLUME: seven client files in, roughly thirty image artefacts moved, every multi image call at or under the ten item cap and no batch above twenty. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no AI object removal, no from scratch generation, and no photograph reaching Express as a URL.
